applicability.scope: Diagnosing training input stalls and choosing bounded queue, shard-cache and cache-ownership changes from DALI, Mosaic Streaming and FFCV, while preserving execution-mode gates, sample ordering and per-host memory budgets and separating remote downloads, local storage reads and host/device transfers
applicability.prerequisites: The pinned readset and its license constraints are read; reading authorizes no commands, cache manipulation or experiment
applicability.input_contract: Dataset format, sample-size distribution, workers and ranks per host, ordering/shuffle, local-cache state and executor mode; a per-host memory budget that includes checkpoint staging and runtime offload; timings that separate remote fetch, decompression/decoding, transformation, batch readiness and device transfer
applicability.produced_artifact: One proposed queue, shard-cache or cache-ownership change with its source-backed rule and boundary, the evidence proposed to confirm it, and a verification contract for a separately authorized comparison; no input-throughput, model-quality or hardware result
failure_modes: Low accelerator utilization is taken to identify which producer stage is late
Missing legacy DALI statistics are read as zero use, or the execution mode is switched silently to obtain them, which changes the comparison
DALI run() returning is read as output-ready timing instead of the outputs() synchronization boundary
Mosaic predownload is treated as a byte cap or request count, or per-worker sample targets are multiplied into an exact network-byte prediction
Look-ahead is increased when the local cache cannot retain the working set, so evicted shards are downloaded again
cache_limit is read as a bound on total process RAM, or the constructor minimum as an optimum or a guarantee against thrashing
An FFCV memory map is taken as proof that its pages are resident
applicability.refusal_point: Rejects changes that violate sample coverage or the stated reproducibility contract even if batches arrive faster, does not report queue depth alone as a performance result, and draws no NPU acceleration claim from the CUDA-oriented DALI source

recommendations: Record dataset format, sample sizes, workers per host, ordering, cache state and executor mode before proposing one change.
Increase Mosaic look-ahead only when readiness starvation is observed and cache headroom exists; otherwise address shard and working-set residency first.
Check the exact DALI configuration surface before use, because the constructor and deserialization paths use different queue keys.
In a later comparison, separate warm-cache throughput from cold retrieval and initialization, and report step time with input wait, host/HBM peaks and actual I/O.
limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.
